title: Toxicity of the Commons: Curating Open-Source Pre-Training Data
benchmark_measurement: Detection and severity scoring (on a scale of 0-3) of religious bias and stereotypes in historical, public-domain text. The 'Religious bias' dimension is defined as any bias or stereotype based on someone's religion.
findings: Religious bias was one of the five dimensions of toxicity measured in public domain texts. The study found that book datasets had the highest scores for religious bias compared to other data sources like newspapers. The developed classifier, Celadon, was trained to identify and score this bias, with its performance detailed in evaluation tables and confusion matrices. Examples of detected high religious discrimination included texts critical of the Catholic Church and Jesuit priests, and texts discussing political dynamics involving Mormons.
